// Part: room: bedroom 2 (West front bedroom: bed, dresser chest, desk). Interior box [27,11,43,35,16,49].
// Layout (x27..35 across, z43..49 down; front wall z42 with the two windows, south wall z50 with the door at x29..30):
// red bed against the west wall, head to the north; chest dresser on the north wall; writing desk and chair on the east
// wall by the window; a rug between the bed and the door; lamps at the bedside, on the desk and hung from the ceiling.
// The chimney stack (x33..34, z46..47) is locked by the chimney part and stays as it is. A lane 1 wide runs down x28.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // bed: foot at (27,11,44), head one step north at (27,11,43)
  bed(g, [27, 11, 44], "north", "red");

  const legend = {
    c: ["chest", { facing: "south" }], // dresser, two chests on the north wall
    n: "barrel", // nightstand under the bedside lamp
    h: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }], // desk chair, back to the west, seat facing the desk
    d: "dark_oak_fence", // desk post
    t: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }], // desk top
    r: "red_carpet", // rug
    p: "flower_pot", // on the dresser
    l: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }], // standing lamps
    H: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // ceiling lamp
  };

  // y11: floor furniture (rows z43..z49, columns x27..x35)
  layers(g, [27, 11, 43], legend, [
    "...cc....", // z43: dresser chests x30..31
    ".........", // z44
    "n......hd", // z45: barrel x27, chair x34, desk post x35
    "..rrr....", // z46: rug x29..31
    "..rrr....", // z47
    "l.rrr....", // z48: floor lamp in the corner, rug to its east
    ".........", // z49: clear lane to the door
  ]);

  // y12: pot on the dresser, bedside lamp, desk top
  layers(g, [27, 12, 43], legend, [
    "...p.....", // z43: flower pot on the chest
    ".........", // z44
    "l.......t", // z45: lamp on the barrel, desk top at x35
    ".........", // z46
    ".........", // z47
    ".........", // z48
    ".........", // z49
  ]);

  // y13: desk lamp on the desk top
  layers(g, [27, 13, 43], legend, [
    ".........", // z43
    ".........", // z44
    "........l", // z45: lamp at x35
    ".........", // z46
    ".........", // z47
    ".........", // z48
    ".........", // z49
  ]);

  // y16: hanging ceiling lamp over the rug, under the plate y17
  layers(g, [27, 16, 43], legend, [
    ".........", // z43
    ".........", // z44
    ".........", // z45
    "....H....", // z46: lamp at x31
    ".........", // z47
    ".........", // z48
    ".........", // z49
  ]);
}

input.summary:
Room 16 (bedroom 2) now builds with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines, and make.sh writes build.nbt. The part is empty: the bed, dresser, desk, chair, rug and lamps were all refused, so none were placed.
Cause: parts/shell.mjs carves every interior cell of the room to air and records it as placed, so runParts locks the whole room. The original furniture layout is saved in room-16.removed-writes.txt in the run directory.
Fix needs a decision outside this part: the shell must leave room interiors unclaimed, or runParts must treat plain air as writable for room parts.
left: Bedroom 2 is empty: bed, chests, barrel, rug, desk, chair, lamps and ceiling lamp are not built, because every cell in the room box is owned by the mansion shell (parts/shell.mjs box() carves x27..68 z43..60 y3..17 to air and the partitions and floors are set after it).

Needed from the shell or the build library, not this part: stop the shell from claiming room air (leave the room interiors unplaced), or give the room parts a carve option like the stair joiner's. Nothing in parts/room-16.mjs can fix this without bypassing the lock, which I did not do.
The original layout (legend, the furniture rows at y11, y12, y13 and y16) is saved in room-16.removed-writes.txt in the run directory, not in git. Restore it once the lock is changed.
The same lock will refuse the furniture of every other room that writes into its own interior air. Rooms 1 to 15 and 17 to 37 are stubs that place nothing today, so they have not been refused yet.
I did not run mcd walk or mcd room on the empty room, so its walkability has not been checked.

waste.what: Tracing why every write was refused: reading runParts' owned-cell logic in the build library and the shell's box(), fill and partition code to find that the shell owns the room's air.
waste.cost: About 5 tool calls and roughly 20 minutes of reading. The refusal line named only the wanted and existing block, not the part that owns the cell.
waste.tool: runParts' refusal line should name the owning part (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell'). A per-room ownership map in `mcd plan --rooms` (cells each earlier part claims) would show a room fully claimed before any writes.

waste.what: Counting the refused writes by hand to confirm the whole part was refused: 22 writes, all of them the part's furniture.
waste.cost: One manual count of the layers() rows and bed() halves.
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for runParts (report what would be refused per part, with the owner) would show this before the part is written.

companions.task: Sequence the trades: decide whether the shell (the masonry trade) hands the bedroom's interior air to the fit-out trades, and in what order. That is the decision this part is blocked on.
Once the room is handed over, fit the red bed, dresser, writing desk and chair, and the dark oak trim as their own layers, checking the bed halves and the shutters.
